hook: Every graph of uncountable edge-connectivity kappa contains a kappa-regular tree with an apex as a minor
summary: In graph theory, a minor is a structure left after deleting and contracting parts of a graph. The authors prove that every graph that stays connected after removing fewer than kappa edges, for uncountable kappa, contains a kappa-regular tree joined to one extra vertex. This extends a countable-case result of Kurkofka. It is a pure existence theorem for infinite graphs.
title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
